clinician.final_diagnosis: an isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) wild-type epithelioid glioblastoma with O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT) methylation at 12% and BRAF V600E mutation
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 60-year-old male presented with a seizure, left-sided numbness, dysarthria, and motor/sensory deficits, with cMRI revealing multifocal lesions in the right temporal lobe and left internal auditory canal (IAC). Surgical resection led to a pathological diagnosis of IDH wild-type epithelioid glioblastoma with O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT) methylation at 12% and BRAF V600E mutation. Adjuvant concomitant chemoradiotherapy was initiated. A cMRI at therapy day 42 showed stable disease in the right temporal lobe but progression of the left IAC lesion. This was followed by rapid clinical deterioration, including new facial nerve weakness, dysphagia, dysarthria, and deafness, necessitating PEG tube placement. Whole brain radiotherapy was subsequently initiated after a lumbar puncture confirmed meningeosis glioblastoma.

Pathology report after surgical resection confirmed an isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) wild-type epithelioid glioblastoma with O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT) methylation at 12% and BRAF V600E mutation.
Patient received adjuvant concomitant chemoradiotherapy including temozolomide and stereotactic radiotherapy of the tumor cavity in the right temporal lobe.
cMRI on therapy day 42 showed the right-sided tumor cavity remained unchanged in size but with a larger perifocal edema, and the lesion in the left IAC was progressive.
Patient developed marked imbalance, rapidly advancing left-sided facial nerve weakness, dysphagia, dysarthria, left-sided deafness, positive Romberg test, and ataxic gait.
A percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) tube was implanted due to persistent dysphagia.
Whole brain radiotherapy was initiated to control the impact of the expanding intracranial mass after lumbar puncture confirmed meningeosis glioblastoma.
